jobs.prompt: Build the replay and compare harness as new modules with tests (do not edit tools/swarm.mjs). Owner rule behind this work: no roadmap item is done until it is benchmarked against real data; every item ships a before and after table; the exit gate is better on its target metric and no regression above 10 percent on the others. Metrics (each reported as measured, estimated or missing, never invented): (1) ready_to_merged_ms per merged ticket; (2) billed_usd and list_usd per merged ticket split into workers, reviews and orchestrator (billed = paid lanes only, list = every job's reported or estimated cost); (3) first_try_pass_rate (jobs complete with zero retries), retries, flaky_failures; (4) owner_interruptions_per_day (decisions, approvals, blockers the owner resolved); (5) idle_slot_pct (slots free while tickets were ready); (6) dirty_tree_incidents, branch_switch_incidents, guard_false_positives; (7) orchestrator_tokens_per_merged_ticket. Create tools/bench-replay.mjs and tools/bench-compare.mjs (SPDX headers, ES modules) and tests. Case format: a case is a JSON file evals/cases/NAME/case.json with {id, title, kind (build, test, docs, migration), prompt, files (repo-relative paths the ticket writes), context (paths), testCommand (argv array), acceptance (list of short lines), scrubbedFrom (a ticket id), sizeBytes}; validateCase(obj) returns plain error strings (required fields, argv array, no absolute paths, no path with .. segments, at most 8 files). scrubCase(raw) removes anything that could be customer data or a secret: it runs every string through tools/security-scan.mjs rules, drops emails and phone numbers and long random tokens, truncates the prompt to 4000 characters, replaces any absolute path with a repo-relative one or removes it, and returns {case, dropped: [{field, kind}]} (kinds only, never values). runReplay({cases, codeRoot, label, parallel, lanes, runner, now}) runs every case with parallel workers at most parallel at a time through the injected async runner(caseObj, {codeRoot, label}) returning {status: 'pass'|'fail'|'error', durationMs, billedUsd, listUsd, retries, tokens, flaky}; the default runner is a stub that throws (the real runner is wired later), so tests use fakes; it returns {label, parallel, startedAt, finishedAt, results: [...], metrics: {pass_rate, first_try_rate, median_ms, p90_ms, billed_usd_per_case, list_usd_per_case, retries_per_case, flaky_rate, throughput_per_min, idle_slot_pct}} where idle_slot_pct is the share of parallel slot time with no case running while cases were still queued, computed from the start and end times; a runner that throws marks that case error and the run continues; concurrency never exceeds parallel (assert it in a test with a fake runner that tracks in-flight count). runLoadSeries({cases, codeRoot, label, levels: [4, 8, 16], runner, now}) runs runReplay at each level and returns the three results plus a table of throughput, pass rate, idle slot percent and flake rate per level. compareReplays(before, after, {target, tolerance = 0.10}) returns {rows: [{metric, before, after, deltaPct, direction: 'better'|'worse'|'same', regression: boolean}], targetImproved: boolean, regressions: [metric], verdict: 'pass'|'fail', reason} where for each metric a lower or higher value is better as known (pass_rate, first_try_rate, throughput_per_min higher is better; median_ms, p90_ms, billed_usd_per_case, list_usd_per_case, retries_per_case, flaky_rate, idle_slot_pct lower is better), a regression is a worsening of more than the tolerance (a zero baseline counts a worsening above 0.01 absolute), the verdict is pass only when the target metric improved and there are no regressions; formatCompareTable(result) returns a plain text table (metric, before, after, change, verdict mark) under 30 lines plus a markdown form formatCompareMarkdown(result) for a PR body. Tests in tests/bench-replay.test.mjs and tests/bench-compare.test.mjs (fake runners, fake clock, no sleeps): case validation and scrubbing (canary email, phone, token and an absolute path never survive; dropped lists kinds only); concurrency bound respected at 4, 8 and 16; a throwing runner yields an error result and the run finishes; idle slot percent from a known schedule; load series produces three levels; compare: target improved with no regressions passes, a 12 percent regression on another metric fails, 9 percent passes, a zero baseline, a missing metric treated as not comparable and listed, table and markdown outputs fit their limits. Write only tools/bench-replay.mjs, tools/bench-compare.mjs, tests/bench-replay.test.mjs and tests/bench-compare.test.mjs. IMPORTANT: the integration secret scan rejected the previous attempt because tests/bench-replay.test.mjs contained a literal that looks like a GitHub token. Never write a token-shaped literal (ghp_, github_pat_, sk-, AKIA, long hex or base64) in any file: when a test needs a fake secret to prove scrubbing, build it at runtime from pieces, for example ["gh","p_"].join("") + "x".repeat(36), so no file contains it.
